purpose: Try to avoid the CPU tree walk by forcing a linear NGRAM tree (external SAM budget 1).
result: Budget 1 yields only one real child then unused siblings; budget 4 yields a main chain of 4 plus a sibling. The tree is inherently irregular, so native MUSA topk=1 linear verify cannot represent it. CPU tree walk remains required and costs more than the draft gain.
conclusion: No usable NGRAM speedup on MUSA without a native topk>1 tree-verify kernel; 160/64K also exceeds the 6GB budget with FP16 KV + verify workspace.
